name: Bank Reconciliation
title: Bank Reconciliation
answer: Bank reconciliation is the process of comparing an organization's internal cash ledger against the bank statement to identify timing differences, errors, and unauthorized transactions. In treasury and liquidity, it underpins the daily cash position and ensures that reported balances are trustworthy before funding, investing, or payment decisions. AI-assisted reconciliation extends this from periodic batch matching to near-continuous comparison across many accounts and currencies. The scope includes not only matching line items but also classifying discrepancies, learning from past resolutions, and flagging unusual patterns that may indicate fraud or operational failure.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Bank reconciliation is the process of comparing an organization's internal cash ledger against the bank statement to identify timing differences, errors, and unauthorized transactions. In treasury and liquidity, it underpins the daily cash position and ensures that reported balances are trustworthy before funding, investing, or payment decisions. AI-assisted reconciliation extends this from periodic batch matching to near-continuous comparison across many accounts and currencies. The scope includes not only matching line items but also classifying discrepancies, learning from past resolutions, and flagging unusual patterns that may indicate fraud or operational failure.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: AI bank reconciliation typically runs inside or alongside an organization's enterprise resource planning system or treasury management system, connected to bank data through file imports, host-to-host connections, or application programming interfaces. The matching engine may be a cloud service or an on-premises module that receives normalized transaction records from both the ledger and the bank. It needs secure storage for historical matches and exception labels, plus a workflow layer for human review. Compute requirements are modest compared with large language models, often handled by standard servers or cloud instances, but data integration and cleansing are the main infrastructure burden.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by first normalizing bank and book transactions into a common format with fields such as date, amount, reference, and counterparty. A rules-based layer applies deterministic matching on exact or near-exact keys, while a learned model scores candidate pairs by similarity and prior resolution patterns. Unmatched or low-confidence items are routed to a review queue where a treasury analyst confirms, splits, or reclassifies them, and that feedback updates the model. Over time the system builds a library of recurring exceptions, such as bank fees, FX timing differences, or intercompany transfers, and can auto-resolve them within defined tolerance limits.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on who can view bank data, who can approve matches, and who can change matching rules or thresholds. Access should follow segregation of duties so that the person preparing reconciliation cannot also approve exceptions or alter the underlying ledger without separate authorization. Provenance requires an audit trail that records the source record, the matched record, the confidence score, and the human or automated action for every cleared item. Model risk arises when the system learns from biased or incomplete exception labels, so periodic review of false positives and false negatives is necessary, and any automated write-off or adjustment must remain subject to policy limits and controller oversight.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Bank reconciliation is moving from daily or weekly batch processing to continuous, event-driven matching as bank application programming interfaces deliver real-time transaction data. The next step is tighter coupling with cash forecasting, where reconciled balances feed liquidity models within minutes rather than hours. AI systems are likely to handle more multi-entity, multi-currency netting and intercompany matching without manual intervention, while humans focus on exceptions that carry payment or compliance risk. Over time, reconciliation may become a background control that supports instant liquidity views and automated funding sweeps, rather than a separate period-end task.
